inputs.original_text: Eight million Americans join anti-Trump protests across US, organisers say An estimated 8 million people gathered at more than 3,300 events across all 50 US states, organisers of the “No Kings” protests said, as demonstrators voiced opposition to President Donald Trump’s leadership. News agency AFP reported that the events were held nationwide, though US authorities have not provided an official count. Organisers said turnout surpassed earlier demonstrations, noting there were “about one million more participants and 600 more events compared to the last No Kings demonstrations in October.”
inputs.modified_text: Organizers say 8 million people joined more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states—about one million more than in October. There’s no official count, so that figure should be treated as an estimate, not proof that everyone agrees. But dismissing mass protest because it isn’t a vote misses the point: peaceful public dissent is one way people hold power accountable between elections. Invoking “law and tradition” to silence protest can protect the status quo, especially when institutions fail to hear people who are already politically marginalized. A loud protest doesn’t govern the country, but neither should those in power mistake their authority for the public’s consent.
